scope: Independent read-only review of root integration snapshot: all19 pathways and23 root tract records. Findings sent to root for correction; source files not edited by this agent.

findings.finding: Read snapshot retained whole-frontal/parietal/temporal and arcuate-is-component claim while corrected origin/target separates frontoparietal SLF from related arcuate. Naming conventions vary; one fixed synonym is too strong.
findings.proposed: Association: bidirectional frontoparietal pathways for attention, working memory and sensorimotor integration; relationships to arcuate depend on anatomical naming convention.

findings.finding: Read snapshot begins lower thoracic/upper lumbar, then gives C8/T1-L2/L3 range, internally omitting caudal cervical/upper thoracic extent.
findings.proposed: Clarke column neurons in caudal cervical/thoracic to upper lumbar cord (approximately C8/T1-L2/L3), receiving lower-body sensory inputs.

findings.finding: Unqualified flexor facilitation/extensor inhibition remains in modality despite function explicitly limiting human evidence.
findings.proposed: Descending somatic motor pathway; flexor-related roles are well described in experimental animals, while the smaller human pathway has an uncertain isolated contribution.

findings.finding: Autonomic somatic motor conflates separately classified autonomic and somatic motor systems. Reticular autonomic networks exist, but this spinal motor bundle should not label them one modality.
findings.proposed: Descending somatic motor: posture, gait, muscle tone and voluntary-movement networks with bilateral influences.

findings.finding: Layer-II/III preferential projections are standard but the supplied Blumenfeld p834 describes layers2/3 generally. Primary monkey tracing provides the more precise preferential rule including deep-layer contributions.
findings.proposed: Predominantly entorhinal layer-II input to dentate/CA3 and mainly layer-III direct input to CA1, with other-layer contributions and parallel routes.
findings.source: Witter & Amaral (1991), monkey tracer anatomy, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/1713237/

findings.finding: New separate arcuate concept can supply an actual record link for dorsal connection; one link should not purport to model all dorsal/ventral routes.
findings.proposed: Link a separate dorsal arcuate step to tract-arcuate-fasciculus and retain unmodeled ventral routes explicitly.

explicit_positive_checks: VOR example leftward head rotation -> right lateral rectus and left medial rectus is correct.
CST crossing in caudal medulla differs from DCML internal arcuate sensory crossing.
Spinothalamic fibres cross near entry in spinal anterior white commissure.
Ventral spinocerebellar second crossing is not the caudal-midbrain SCP output decussation.
Corticopontine neurons terminate mainly ipsilateral; separate pontocerebellar neurons cross.
Papez text explicitly notes omitted direct fornix-to-anterior-thalamus route.
The Nambu2000 hyperdirect source is an actual primary monkey physiology paper and matches cortex-STN-pallidal excitation.
Descending oculosympathetic route is mainly ipsilateral and pre/postganglionic relays are distinguished.
limits: Independent review catches substantive residual inconsistencies; it is not a claim that every low-level physiological claim or every source range was independently replicated. Does not quantify tract dimensions or validate anatomy against registered patient imaging.
